heading: மொழிபெயர்ப்பு
lines: Lend your ears
O lass with lustrous bracelets!
The youth of unrestrained play,
Who'd tread down the little sand-houses we built on street,
Who'd cut off the wreaths our tresses wore,
Who'd run off with our streaky play balls
Causing annoyance to us thereof,
There came to our house ere on a day
As mother and I were in,
And uttered the words:
'O the folk inside!
I've quite a thirst!'
Thereat mother said:
'O my bright jewell'd lass!
Take water in the gold-leafed bowl
And get him quench his thirst'.
And I went out (holding water in hand)
Knowing not the lad that he was;
He seized my forearm bracelets adorned
And held it fast causing pain;
Dismayed I did cry out:
'O mother see what this man's done!'
Mother came out running in anxiety felt,
I said 'He hiccoughed as he drank';
And mother went about
Stroking him over and over,
And the thief of that man
Cast his oblique glance radiant
As if dispossessing my soul,
And extended thus his passion's bond.
